name: presubmit
description: Catches the common manuscript submission mistakes before a journal does. Checks sections, author/affiliation/email completeness, abstract length and keyword counts, reference problems (duplicates by DOI or text, missing years, malformed DOIs, citations with no matching reference, references never cited), missing ethics/disclosure statements, and deterministic language/typography errors. Also catches what an editorial round actually flags: placeholders and unresolved tracked changes or comments left in the submitted .docx, a declared word count over the format's limit, more references than the format allows, effect estimates reported without a confidence interval, trials named only by acronym, the same study described twice, and the authors' own ongoing study promoted in the conclusion. A reviewer-anticipation category adds 147 rules distilled from thirteen referee cohorts, the author's own plus 38 open-peer-review manuscripts from PeerJ and F1000Research (608 referee objections): a review with no reproducible search, 'systematic' with no machinery, effect sizes with no table, no limitations, causal verbs on observational data, an unsourced numeric target, a recommendation the text itself calls unvalidated, an own trial with no registration, undefined abbreviations, doubled reference entries, AI use with unverified references, survey and primary-study methods guards, simulation-only performance figures, odds and risk ratios in one pool, a two-trial estimate with no qualifier, a sensitivity result left out of the abstract, machine screening with no measured check, a Hungarian manuscript citing no Hungarian literature. Reads .docx/.pdf/.tex/.txt including field-managed EndNote files (English and Hungarian headings), applies a journal profile (Cureus, Annals Ideas and Opinions and Orvosi Hetilap built in), and prints a severity-ranked readiness report with fix hints. An advisory style category flags the tells of an AI-assisted draft (adapted from academic-humanizer, MIT), and /presubmit:humanize rewrites them out while a deterministic invariants check proves no number, citation, equation or cross-reference was lost. Offline and deterministic by default — no language model, no spell dictionary, so no false positives on medical terms; an opt-in --online flag additionally asks PubMed whether any cited paper has been corrected or retracted.
